text:
elaine: Quick heads-up from today's UX pass — keyboard flow in the Metrics dashboard table is funky when you expand a row. Steps: Console > Metrics > Expand row, use Arrow keys to move, press Enter to open details. After expand the focus ring disappears and pressing Tab jumps to the toolbar instead of the expanded content.

rohith: confirmed on Win10 + NVDA. I think the expand action replaces the row node (virtualization) and we lose the focused element. The SR then reads something like "Row 3" instead of the detail header.

morgan: also repro on mac + VoiceOver. Behavior inconsistent when reduced-motion is on — animation seems to influence whether focus is preserved.

elaine: two issues to attack: 1) keep focus visible and programmatically move it into the detail pane after open, and 2) ensure SR announces the new region.

rohith: propose we: a) maintain a stable focusable container for the list (role=listbox) and b) on open use focus() to land on the detail panel's first interactive element, then add an aria-live polite message like "Details for request 123 opened".

morgan: +1. Also let's avoid relying solely on outline-offset + shadow for focus state; add an explicit 2px stroke for contrast. I can paste a CSS patch: 
```
.list-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b63ff; outline-offset: 3px; }
.detail-panel:focus { box-shadow: none; border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, #0b63ff 85%, black 15%); }
```

elaine: thanks. Small accessibility caveat: VoiceOver does not always respect programmatic focus during animations. We might need to wait for the open animation to finish (or disable it when reduced-motion is set) before calling focus().

rohith: agreed. Implementation plan: check prefers-reduced-motion and, if false, wait for transitionend before focus(); if true, focus immediately. Add tests for both.

morgan: also think about virtualization: unmounting offscreen items is fine, but when the detail pane references the original row (aria-labelledby) ensure the id exists (do not rely on ephemeral DOM id generation). Use stable ids like `data-row-id="metrics-<id>"` and mirror in aria-labelledby.

a11y-bot: Scan result: focus-retention-check FAILED. Suggested test cases: keyboard-only expand, SR announce after expand, reduced-motion focus timing. See /logs/a11y/1747609999-metrics-expand.log

elaine: great. rohith can you make a micro-PR with: stable list container role change, focus handoff logic with reduced-motion guard, aria-live announcement, and a visible 2px focus style? Put behind an FF.

rohith: will do. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821 (WIP)  contains tests + a11y notes. I'll run NVDA + VoiceOver locally and attach recordings.

morgan: when you open the PR, add a small checklist for reviewers: 
- preserves virtualization perf
- focus visible for high-contrast themes
- SR announcement present and correct
- reduced-motion behavior validated

devops: FYI if this introduces a CSS var we need to ship with a fallback for older browsers. Also watch bundle size if adding polyfills.

elaine: perfect. tagging @morgan for design review + @a11y-bot for re-run after PR. We'll dogfood canary with folks who use SR for a day. :eyes:
